stories.title: Addison Lee founder owes £20.5m in tax after UK tribunal ruling
stories.summary: A UK tax tribunal ruled that Addison Lee's founder owes HMRC £20.5 million in unpaid tax. The ruling represents a significant enforcement win for HMRC in a high-profile tax avoidance case.

stories.title: Government expands crackdown on knife crime
stories.summary: The Home Office announced an expansion of its knife crime crackdown, introducing new enforcement measures. The announcement comes as part of the government's continued focus on violence reduction.

stories.title: 'Outright racist' activist Daniel Thomas will face 'full force of law', says Home Secretary
stories.summary: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood condemned anti-asylum activist Daniel Thomas as 'outright racist', warning he will face the full force of the law for any criminal acts. The comments follow controversy over his activities near asylum seeker accommodation sites.

stories.title: UK paying £56,000 for each person returned to France under 'one in one out' scheme
stories.summary: The UK is paying approximately £56,000 per individual returned to France under a bilateral returns agreement. The scheme is part of efforts to deter small boat Channel crossings.

stories.title: UK ODA Spend 2025: Final international development statistics published
stories.summary: The FCDO published final UK Official Development Assistance (ODA) figures for 2025, providing a comprehensive breakdown of UK foreign aid expenditure. The release covers all major development spending streams across partner countries.

stories.title: Anti-money laundering and asset recovery strategy 2026–2029 released
stories.summary: The government published its new anti-money laundering and asset recovery strategy covering 2026 to 2029. The strategy focuses on disrupting criminal networks operating on UK high streets and internationally, aiming to recover more criminal assets.

stories.title: DWP publishes research on supporting employers to recruit disabled people
stories.summary: The Department for Work and Pensions released new research exploring how employers can be better supported to recruit disabled people and those with health conditions. The report makes recommendations for improving workplace inclusion and reducing disability employment gaps.

stories.title: Government unveils Nature Restoration Fund plan to unlock over 15,000 new homes in Norfolk
stories.summary: DEFRA unveiled the first plan under the new Nature Restoration Fund, designed to help deliver up to 15,780 new homes in Norfolk while protecting natural habitats. The fund aims to unlock housing development that might otherwise be blocked by environmental constraints.

stories.title: Family Food FYE 2025 annual report published
stories.summary: DEFRA released its annual Family Food report covering the financial year ending 2025, providing data on household food and drink purchasing trends across the UK. The report tracks changes in nutrition, spending, and food security.

stories.title: Remote monitoring update for Environmental Land Management agreements
stories.summary: DEFRA's Rural Payments Agency published an update on how remote monitoring technology is being used to support Environmental Land Management (ELM) scheme agreements. The technology enables more efficient verification of land stewardship activities.

stories.title: Army to receive new ISR 'spy' drones in deals worth up to £416m
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence announced two contracts worth up to £416 million for new Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) drones for the British Army. The package includes Tekever AR5 aircraft and over 1,000 smaller drones to enhance battlefield awareness.

stories.title: UK allocates £300 million for military AI programmes through 2030
stories.summary: The UK has committed £300 million in dedicated funding for military artificial intelligence programmes between 2026–27 and 2029–30. The investment signals a major push to integrate AI capabilities across defence operations.

agencies.name: BIST
agencies.description: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

stories.title: MPs tell ministers to find credible plan for British Steel as costs soar
stories.summary: A parliamentary committee warned ministers to urgently produce a credible plan for British Steel after costs described as 'startling' continued to rise. The spending watchdog is scrutinising the government's handling of the nationalised steelmaker.

stories.title: Life Sciences sector attracts over £3 billion in new public-private investment
stories.summary: The UK Life Sciences sector secured over £3 billion in new public-private investment over the past 12 months, reflecting strong international confidence in UK science and innovation. BIST highlighted the milestone as evidence of the UK's competitiveness as a science superpower.

stories.title: International Trade Week 2026 confirmed for 9–13 November
stories.summary: BIST confirmed International Trade Week 2026 will run from Monday 9 to Friday 13 November, connecting UK businesses with global opportunities. The week-long event brings together exporters, investors, and trade advisers.

stories.title: NHS waiting lists rise for fourth month in a row
stories.summary: NHS England data shows the number of people waiting for planned treatment rose for the fourth consecutive month, with nearly 709,700 cases in July including over 4,700 waiting more than two years. The figures raise concerns about the government's NHS recovery targets.

stories.title: Plans to limit NHS ADHD diagnoses attacked as 'rationing' healthcare
stories.summary: Proposals to restrict NHS diagnoses of ADHD have drawn strong criticism from patient groups and clinicians who say it amounts to rationing of healthcare. Critics argue the plans would leave thousands without access to assessment and treatment.

stories.title: World Patient Safety Day 2026: NHS Supply Chain highlights digital safety improvements
stories.summary: On World Patient Safety Day, NHS Supply Chain highlighted progress on digital capabilities and data visibility to improve patient safety. New programmes aim to identify supply chain risks earlier and strengthen procurement resilience.

stories.title: Royal Mail under investigation for delivery failures across Merseyside
stories.summary: Royal Mail is facing an investigation into delivery failures affecting 11 postcode areas across Merseyside. The probe adds to growing regulatory scrutiny over the company's ability to meet its service commitments.

stories.title: Royal Mail delivery problems in Worcester prompt MP to demand government action
stories.summary: Widespread delivery failures in Worcester have prompted the city's MP to formally call on the government to intervene and hold Royal Mail accountable. Residents report significant delays and missed deliveries across the city.

stories.title: Royal Mail delays in Milton Keynes and Bletchley spark MP calls for action
stories.summary: MPs representing Milton Keynes and Bletchley constituencies have called for action over persistent Royal Mail delivery delays in their areas. From April 2026, Royal Mail's regulated targets changed to 90% first-class next-day delivery and 95% second-class within three weekdays.
